title: Mexico’s GDP Records Strongest Growth Since 2023: 3.3% Year-on-Year in the Third Quarter
author: Denisse Torres Hernández
content:
_This article by[Denisse Torres
Hernández](https://www.sinembargo.mx/author/denissetorres/) originally
appeared in the [November 23, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4908306/el-pib-de-mexico-logra-mayor-
crecimiento-desde-2023-3-3-anual-en-tercer-trimestre/), a Mexican digital news
outlet._

_Services led economic growth with a quarterly increase of 1.2 percent, ahead
of industry and agricultural activities._

**Mexico City, November 23 (SinEmbargo).-** **Mexico’s** **Gross Domestic
Product** (**GDP**) grew **3.3 percent year-on-year** during the **third
quarter of 2026** , its strongest increase since the second quarter of 2023,
when it recorded the same growth, according to figures published this Monday
by the [**National Institute of Statistics and Geography**
(**INEGI**)](https://www.sinembargo.mx/tag/inegi/).

During the third quarter, economic activity grew 0.9 percent compared with the
previous three months and outpaced the rate in the same period of 2025, driven
by increases across all the country’s [**economic**
**activities**](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4908309/la-actividad-economica-
avanzo-3-anual-y-cayo-0-7-mensual-en-septiembre-dice-inegi/), although some
grew faster than others.

> The president of [**INEGI**](https://www.inegi.org.mx/), Graciela Márquez
> Colín, shared the results on social media: "In the third quarter of 2026,
> using seasonally adjusted figures, it recorded the following changes: 0.9
> percent quarter-on-quarter and 3.3 percent year-on-year.”

> [Post by @GMarquezColin on
> X](https://x.com/GMarquezColin/status/2124837518524682628)

## Services Lead GDP Growth

As the economy’s main driver, services - which include areas such as trade,
transportation, education and finance - grew 1.2 percent compared with the
second quarter and 3.6 percent compared with the previous year.

For secondary activities, primarily related to industry, growth was 0.4
percent quarter-on-quarter and 2.7 percent year-on-year. Meanwhile, primary
activities, which include agriculture, livestock farming, fishing and
forestry, grew 0.3 and 1.5 percent, respectively.

> “For this period, by economic activity group, the quarterly changes were:
> 1.2 percent in tertiary activities, 0.4 percent in secondary activities, 0.3
> percent in primary activities,” Márquez Colín wrote about each sector’s
> performance when sharing the
> [report](https://www.inegi.org.mx/contenidos/saladeprensa/boletines/2026/pibt/pib_Pconst2026_11.pdf).

> [Post by @INEGI_INFORMA on
> X](https://x.com/INEGI_INFORMA/status/2124836361140126029)

The data confirm that trade and services maintained the highest growth rate
both compared with the previous quarter and year-on-year, marking their
largest gap with agriculture and livestock farming, which grew just 1.5
percent over the past year.

Over the first nine months of 2026, GDP recorded real growth of 1.9 percent
compared with the same period of the previous year. However, performance
varied across sectors: services grew 2.5 percent and secondary activities, 1.1
percent.

By contrast, agricultural activities recorded a decline of 0.9 percent over
the first nine months of the year, as third-quarter growth proved insufficient
to offset previous losses.

[Read the original INEGI report

## Construction Stands Out Within Industry

Within secondary activities, construction recorded year-on-year growth of
seven percent during the third quarter, while manufacturing industries grew
1.9 percent.

Wholesale trade led services growth, expanding 12 percent year-on-year,
followed by retail trade at 3.7 percent and health care and social assistance
services at 3.1 percent.

By contrast, the hotel and restaurant sector suffered a year-on-year decline
of 2.2 percent, while professional, scientific and technical services fell 0.8
percent.
